defaults.rule: Always run step-00-preflight.md first — verifies `pgbx` is on PATH and picks the profile; backup routes also run `pgbx doctor --json`. No mutation may run before this.
Read-only questions (route query, memory) need NO doctor and NO pgbx extension: pgbx is a plain Postgres client too. A reply with `backups: "off"` is normal, not an error.
Use this file as the intent router. Family files (status.md, backup.md, …) hold recipes; step files hold cross-cutting flows.
Always pass `--json`. With SQL fallback use `psql -XAtq` and single-row statements.
Safety tiers in workflow.md decide whether you act, ask, or require explicit approval. Destructive gates are enforced in code; never bypass them.

TIE-BREAK: when more than one route matches, the route whose matched phrase is LONGEST wins — "backup before deploy" (backup-before-deploy) beats "backup" (backup). Only if two matched phrases are the same length, ask the user which they meant.

flow-control.rule: If preflight fails (pgbx missing and no psql access), surface the install text and STOP.
After every recipe response, stop and wait. Do not auto-chain into the next intent.

route.when: is postgres backed up, is it backed up, backup status, are backups working, last backup, list backups, show backups, when was the last backup, pgbx status, pgbx list, job queue, why hasn't my backup started, how long will the backup take, pgbx jobs, cancel the backup, is the server busy, load gate, pgbx load
route.goal: Answer "are we backed up?" in one line per database, from status JSON.

route.when: how big is the database, table sizes, how many connections, run a select, run a query, query the database, how many rows, show me the tables, which tables, connect to the database, connect over ssh, through the jump host, via the bastion, through ssm, cloud sql, azure bastion, postgres client, pgbx query
route.goal: Answer a read question with `pgbx query` JSON through the profile (adapter included: ssh, aws, gcp, azure or the user's own); works without the pgbx extension.

steps.step: Pick the profile; read the database memory. No doctor.

route.when: remember this, remember that, put it here, save this query, save the query as, note the tables, remember the schema, what do you remember, forget that, clear the memory
route.goal: Read or append the database's own memory files; create them only because the user asked.

route.when: take a backup, backup now, back up the database, backup the server, snapshot the database, pgbx now
route.goal: Queue a backup, wait for it, return the backup id and S3 key.

route.when: backup before deploy, backup before migration, safe to deploy, pre-deploy backup, before i run the migration
route.goal: Health → backup → wait → verify → report id, before a risky change.

route.when: restore the db, restore the database, recover deleted rows, undo the migration, restore into a new database, get yesterday's data back, pgbx db-restore
route.goal: Restore one database into a NEW database; the live one is untouched.

route.when: restore on a new server, restore to a new server, server is gone, lost the server, restore from s3, restore the server from backup, restore the whole server, pgbx backups --from-s3, db-restore --from-s3
route.goal: Old server lost: list dumps in S3 and restore each database into a NEW database on the new server (no extension needed there).

steps.step: Confirm pgbx (S3 commands need no running extension).

route.rule: Never read or print the credentials file. Renaming a restored database over a live one is destructive and needs explicit approval.

route.when: postgres is down, postgres won't start, postgres crashed, database is down, disk full, disk is full, no space left on device, wal growing, pg_wal is huge, pg_wal growing, wal backlog, out of memory, oom killed, too many connections, server is corrupted, pgbx diagnose
route.goal: Name why Postgres is down or WAL/disk is growing, then walk the printed steps by safety tier. Diagnose first; restore only if the diagnosis says so.

steps.step: Confirm pgbx (doctor works with Postgres down and embeds the diagnosis).

route.rule: pgbx never runs a remedy. Never delete files in pg_wal/, base/, global/ or pg_xact/. Destructive steps need explicit human approval of that exact step.

route.when: verify the backup, restore test, can we actually restore, is the backup good, verification failed, pgbx verify
route.goal: Prove the newest backup restores; explain any failure.

route.when: change backup schedule, backup every hour, retention, keep backups for, pause backups, resume backups, stop backups for now, when should backups run, suggest a schedule, quietest time to back up, pgbx schedule suggest
route.goal: Change schedule, retention, pause/resume; ask first when protection shrinks.

route.when: exclude table from backup, skip rows, data scope, backup only some tables, which tables are backed up without rows
route.goal: Decide whose rows are kept; table definitions are always backed up.

route.when: download the backup, download link, give me the dump file, presigned url, who can run backups, grant backup access
route.goal: Time-limited link to one backup, or role grants.

route.when: audit ui, audit trail, audit log, backup dashboard, backup web ui, open the ui, who did what, who changed the backups, who paused backups, who downloaded the backup, backup timeline, pgbx ui
route.goal: Start the read-only audit UI as a viewer login (or answer from its JSON), never with an admin/superuser role.
route.rule: The UI is read-only; creating the viewer login role and exposing it beyond 127.0.0.1 are the human's call.

route.when: backup failing, backups are failing, why did the backup fail, pgbx doctor, pgbx logs, backup error, queued forever
route.goal: Name the cause and the plain-language fix from doctor and logs.
